name: Pin-to-Net-to-Symbol Mapper
blurb: trace an MCU pin to its PCB net and its firmware symbol
intro: Paste the board netlist (KiCad .net or CSV) and the firmware's pin definitions (CubeMX main.h, #define / const, Zephyr devicetree). Each MCU pin is joined to its net and to the firmware symbol on the same port and number, flagging pins the firmware drives that go nowhere, symbols for pins the MCU does not have, and connected GPIOs the firmware never names.

inputs.label: Netlist (KiCad .net or CSV ref,pin,name,net)
inputs.help: KiCad: File > Export > Netlist (KiCad format), paste the file. CSV: one row per pin, ref,pin,pin name,net.

inputs.label: MCU reference
inputs.help: Empty = the part with the most GPIO-named pins.

inputs.label: Firmware pin definitions

#define BTN_USER_GPIO_Port GPIOA
#define LED_Pin GPIO_PIN_5
#define LED_GPIO_Port GPIOA
#define IMU_INT_Pin GPIO_PIN_0
#define IMU_INT_GPIO_Port GPIOB
#define DBG_TOGGLE_Pin GPIO_PIN_3
#define DBG_TOGGLE_GPIO_Port GPIOB
#define SPARE_Pin GPIO_PIN_15
#define SPARE_GPIO_Port GPIOD

/* board.h */
#define I2C_SCL_PIN   PB6
#define I2C_SDA_PIN   PB7
#define UART_TX_PIN   PA9
#define UART_RX_PIN   PA10
inputs.help: main.h / board.h / pins.h defines and consts, or a devicetree overlay with gpios = <&gpioa 5 ...>.

inputs.label: Bare numbers mean
inputs.help: Whether LED_PIN = 2 means GPIO2. Only pin-like names (LED, SDA, _PIN...) up to 60 are read.

usage: Give netlist as KiCad netlist text or CSV (ref,pin,name,net), mcu as the reference designator, firmware as the pin definition source text, numbers = none | gpio (whether bare integers are GPIO numbers), and an optional query (pin number, pin name, net or symbol). It returns one row per MCU pin with its net, firmware symbol, the other pins on that net and a status (ok, names differ, not in firmware, firmware uses an unconnected pin, power), the firmware symbols that name no pin of the MCU, a single-line trace when the query matches one pin, and a CSV of the map. Use it to check a board and its firmware agree before bring-up or after a pin swap.
sources: KiCad netlist export format (s-expression, 'export' version E; nets with node ref/pin/pinfunction/pintype)
STM32CubeMX generated main.h user label defines (<label>_Pin / <label>_GPIO_Port)
Zephyr devicetree GPIO specifier (gpios = <&gpioX pin flags>)
Rule of thumb: net and symbol names that share no word are a likely swap
